h: The four causes of old age, and the questions

p: — old age leaps upon a person
— "for he was terrified by the sword," etc.,
— and what is written after it?
— about preparing the building of the Temple.
— that from the strain of war
— for the verse "And Joshua was old," etc.,
— "And it came to pass, many days after … round about,"

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Chayei Sara 2 (on Genesis 24:1): "Because of four things old age leaps upon a person: because of fear, because of the anger caused by children, because of a bad wife, and because of wars … but Abraham … therefore it is written of him, 'and the Lord blessed Abraham in all.'" The Midrash gives the order David, Eli, Joshua, Solomon, which is what Rav Tzadok asks about. The whole maamar reads this Midrash: each of the four "causes" is a path by which a person becomes a zaken, one who has acquired wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Joshua 13:1 and Joshua 23:1. In 13:1, "Joshua was old, advanced in days" comes right after the list of conquered kings in chapter 12. In 23:1: "It came to pass, many days after the Lord had given Israel rest from all their enemies round about, that Joshua was old, advanced in days." The Tanchuma cites 23:1. Rav Tzadok points out that Joshua is already called old in 13:1, right after the conquest, so the old age did not come from the strain of war. Paragraph 6 gives his answer: it was the conquest itself.

p: — But the matter of old age is this:
— points to the elders of the congregation
— This is as they said in the Gemara:
, — "zaken — zeh kanah, this one has acquired."
— It indicates that he acquired the wisdom
— and also that it is manifest,
— that one can point to it with a finger,
— as in the Time to Come
— when wisdom is engraved on the heart permanently,

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 32b: "'Zaken' means only a sage … R. Yose HaGelili says: 'zaken' means only one who has acquired wisdom." Rav Tzadok reads the derashah as the notarikon zaken = zeh kanah ("this one acquired"). He hears two ideas in it: kanah, possession, and zeh, something that can be pointed at.

p: — And this is the meaning of
— what they said in the Gemara
— "A sage is greater than a prophet."
— at the Oral Torah in its truth,
— and that is through the holy spirit,
— That is: although they do not attain it
— but it shines forth in the heart
— he is greater than a prophet;
— through a lens that does not shine,
— as one pointing with a finger,
— which is of the level of
— where a maidservant saw at the Sea

— And this is what they said,
— "a sage is greater than a prophet":
— the level of "this one acquired wisdom,"
— And this is the meaning of what it said,

h: David: fear, the Temple and the Ark

— was a chariot for the attribute of Malchut —
— And this is why they said,
— for it is written "for he was terrified," etc.,
— and afterward the passage is written
— of how he made the preparations
— the Sanctuary of the Lord God,

— to bring the Ark of the covenant of the Lord," etc.;
— and the Ark is in the Holy of Holies,
— where there is the revelation of

h: Joshua: the wars and the Land of Israel

p: — That is: in the Land of Israel
— And the essence of the Oral Torah
— is in the Land of Israel,
— like the Torah of the Land of Israel,
— like the wisdom of the Land of Israel.
— And this is what they said
, — for it is the inventory of the Land of Israel."
— the whole root of the Oral Torah
— from the five books of the Torah.
— is to bring out the holy sparks,
— along the lines of what is written,
, — "and You give life to them all."
— "so that there be added to them," etc.;
— who held no rule in the Land
— "And Joshua was old, advanced in days":
— it became clear that he attained
— that he acquired wisdom as a possession,
— by its being fixed in the heart
— and refined in all the attributes.
— even if Israel would go astray,
— they will merit to bring out
— and will merit all the light
— of the Oral Torah as a possession,
— in the aspect and level of "this one acquired."

h: Solomon: the bad wife and teshuvah

p: — "because of a bad wife," from Solomon,
— for it is written, "And it was in the time of Solomon's old age
— that his wives turned away his heart," etc.
— That is: first it is written,
— "and his wives turned away his heart,"
— "And it was in the time of Solomon's old age
— that his wives turned away his heart," etc.,
, — like the heart of David his father."
— what is said at the Giving of the Torah,
— And so here it is written
— and he did not notice until later,
— then he took it to heart at once
— who raised up the yoke of teshuvah,"
— he would have been the Messiah.
— But his heart was not whole
— like the heart of David his father.
— he attained the trait of old age —
— and that the Name Havayah be his God,
— with the thorn-tip of the Yud,
— that even one who went so far astray
— as with King Solomon, peace be upon him,
— whom they even sought to count
— who have no share in the World to Come,
— מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ כֹּחַ זֶה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
— until he attains the trait of old age —

paragraphs.text: I Kings 11:3–4: "and his wives turned away his heart" and "it came to pass in Solomon's old age that his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not whole with the Lord his God like the heart of David his father." This is the Tanchuma's proof text for "a bad wife." Rav Tzadok reads the two stages of the verse as a sequence: Solomon did not notice, then noticed and did teshuvah. The print here reads "shinav hittu" ("his teeth turned"); it is corrected to "nashav hittu" ("his wives turned").

p: — with his sending to take a wife for Isaac,
, — from the daughters of the Canaanite.
— that if he took from the daughters of Canaan,
— For concerning Esau he was told
— when the soul of Jacob came forth,
— is not counted as his seed.
אֲבָל אִם לֹא הָיָה לוֹקֵחַ אֶת רִבְקָה
— But had he not taken Rivkah,
— and the dross had come out
— his seed would not have merited
— Abraham our father, peace be upon him, attained
— And so Abraham our father merited
— the land of the seven nations,
— and attain "the inventory of the Land of Israel";
— and if they do not go astray,
— and if they will need exiles,
וְכֵן זָכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
— And so Abraham our father, peace be upon him, merited
— that even one who goes far astray,
— since he comes from the seed of Jacob,
— King Solomon, peace be upon him,
— for through her he was aroused
— And this is what is said,
— "And the Lord blessed Abraham in all"
— in all the levels, as said.
